t: The Cotton library is a manuscript collection, and what you're standing near is its story rather than a single building. It takes its name from Sir Robert Cotton, an antiquarian and bibliophile who lived from 1571 to 1631, a Member of Parliament and the man who founded it. His collection became one of the three foundation collections of the British Museum in 1753. Today it is one of the major collections of the Department of Manuscripts at the British Library.
